control._comment: bin/dashd-control -- mobile-facing config surface (#30). Binds LAN-reachable (unlike server.host above), so every route past /api/health requires the pairing token; qr.svg/rotate are loopback-only regardless of token.

logs._comment: Log-highlighter panel (#28), source editable from the Control Backend. source_type is 'journalctl' or 'file'. journalctl_matches are raw journal field matches, OR'd together -- they match on the PROCESS rather than the unit because local auth failures come from cosmic-greeter/greetd/sudo spread across several units, including per-session session-N.scope names that cannot be hardcoded, so no single unit catches a failed login (#72). Indexed field matches, never --grep: a system-wide grep is a full text scan and measured 4.3s even bounded to 24h, versus 126ms here. journalctl_unit is the Control Backend's phone-editable override and WINS when set -- clear it (null) to return to the broad matches below.

projects._comment: Projects panel (#62) -- per-repo GitHub issue stats from one `gh api graphql` call covering the authenticated user plus every org they belong to. Owners are always discovered, never listed here (a hand-kept list goes stale the moment an org is joined); exclude_owners only trims. refresh_seconds is deliberately hours -- this is a standing reminder of outstanding work, not a live metric -- and the fetch runs on a background thread so a slow `gh` never stalls /api/state. stale_after_days hides repos untouched that long, keeping dormant projects off the card; 0 disables the cutoff.

updates._comment: Pending apt-get upgrade counts (#83) -- `apt-get -s upgrade` (a read-only simulation against the local apt cache, no network, no root) measured ~4s on this machine, so it runs on a background thread and is cached the same fetch-once way Projects is. refresh_seconds is hours: apt's own cache refreshes on its own cadence already, so polling faster than that would just re-measure the same numbers.

sessions._comment: Sessions panel (#71) -- who logged in since the last boot, read from systemd-logind's journal. NOT utmp/wtmp: the COSMIC greeter writes no user utmp record, so `last`/`who` see nothing on this machine. The list resets at every boot because the read is scoped with `journalctl -b`; there is no stored history to prune, unlike metrics.db. min_uid is the retroactive human-sessions-only filter -- a closed session has no logind object left to test Class=user against, but its uid separates the same set, and it drops the uid-988 cosmic-greeter session that opens and closes at every single boot. max_rows caps the panel; 0 disables the cap.

weather_alerts._comment: Weather panel highlight (#46). temp_high_f/rain_pct compare directly against weather.temp/precip_prob, which are already in units.temperature/units above -- assumes fahrenheit, matching this config's units. condition_patterns are regex over weather.desc, same {regex, label} shape as logs.patterns above; first match wins. aqi_high (#79) compares against air_quality.aqi (US AQI scale); 101 is the first "Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups" value.

display._tint_strength_comment: Multiplier over web/app.js's TINT_PHASES alphas (#88, follow-up to #78's surface tint which was calibrated to invisible). A selection (#74), same as theme -- edit here only to change the shipped default; a live pick from the context menu's Tint submenu persists to data/config.local.json instead. 1 == Medium (web/app.js's TINT_STRENGTHS), the baseline TINT_PHASES were tuned against; 0 == Off, genuinely no paint.

outputs._comment: Per-output layout overrides. Key = monitor model or connector as reported by the host (see `dashd-host --list`). 'layout' picks a top-level layout in web/app.js; omit an output to use 'auto'.
